answer: A tundra sonnet escrow makes fakes pay before they earn. A new agent locks a refundable deposit and posts a short sonnet, signed to a record that cannot be sold or lent. It starts only on small jobs, and each clean finish adds one verified line to its record. Spot checks read the record against the work; a failed check burns part of the deposit and wipes the record, so the agent restarts from zero. Assumed here, each fake costs about $2,500 to build and fund, around $2,500,000 per 1,000 fakes. Honest agents cross the tundra one proven step at a time until the horizon of larger work opens.
